title: The 'Right to Disconnect'
topic_description: Recent studies in Hong Kong indicate that 75% of secondary school students feel "anxious" if they do not check their social media notifications within 15 minutes. In response, some European countries have passed a "Right to Disconnect" law, allowing students and employees to ignore all school or work-related messages after 8:00 PM to protect their mental wellbeing. Critics argue this might reduce Hong Kong's global competitiveness, while supporters claim it is essential to prevent burnout.
discussion_points: The negative effects of being 'always-on' for students.
Whether a 'Right to Disconnect' policy should be implemented in your school.
Practical ways students can manage their digital wellbeing without a law.
Any other related ideas you think are important.

candidates.A: The Pragmatist: Agrees with the 'competitive' argument. Argues that in a fast-paced city like HK, being unreachable is a disadvantage.
candidates.B: The Empath: Focuses on sleep deprivation and the 'fear of missing out' (FOMO). Strongly supports the law.
candidates.C: The Sceptic: Believes a law is too much 'red tape.' Thinks self-discipline is the only real solution.

individual_response_questions: Do you think parents should have the right to check their children's phones?
Tell us about one app you couldn't live without and why.
Some people say social media makes us more lonely. Do you agree?
If you were given $10,000 to delete all your social media for a year, would you do it?
